questions.prompt: How much heat is required to warm \(2.0\,\mathrm{kg}\) of material with \(c=500\,\mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}\,K^{-1}}\) by \(10\,\mathrm{K}\)?
A \(0.40\,\mathrm{kg}\) object absorbs \(1200\,\mathrm{J}\) and its temperature rises by \(6.0\,\mathrm{K}\). Find its specific heat capacity.
An object loses \(850\,\mathrm{J}\) of heat. What is the sign of \(Q\) if the object is the system?
questions.answer:
Heat removed from the chosen system is negative:
\[
Q=-850\,\mathrm{J}
\]

questions.prompt: Find the temperature rise of \(0.25\,\mathrm{kg}\) of aluminum with \(c=900\,\mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}\,K^{-1}}\) when it absorbs \(4.5\times10^3\,\mathrm{J}\).
A \(3.0\,\mathrm{kg}\) block has heat capacity \(2400\,\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}\). Find its specific heat capacity.
questions.answer:
The object's heat capacity is \(C=mc\), so
\[
c=\frac{C}{m}=\frac{2400}{3.0}=800\,\mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}\,K^{-1}}
\]

questions.prompt: A heater supplies \(150\,\mathrm{W}\) to \(0.60\,\mathrm{kg}\) of water with \(c=4190\,\mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}\,K^{-1}}\). Ignoring losses, find the initial rate of temperature rise.
A copper sample and a water sample have the same mass and absorb the same heat. Copper has a smaller specific heat capacity than water. Which has the larger temperature rise? Explain.
questions.answer:
For the same \(Q\) and \(m\),
\[
\Delta T=\frac{Q}{mc}
\]
The smaller \(c\) gives the larger temperature rise. Copper warms more than water for the same heat input per kilogram.

questions.prompt: A \(0.50\,\mathrm{kg}\) component with \(c=700\,\mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}\,K^{-1}}\) generates thermal energy internally at \(18\,\mathrm{W}\) while losing heat to the surroundings at \(10\,\mathrm{W}\). Find \(dT/dt\).

A material sample of mass \(0.30\,\mathrm{kg}\) is heated electrically at \(24\,\mathrm{W}\). Its temperature rises from \(22\,{}^\circ\mathrm{C}\) to \(30\,{}^\circ\mathrm{C}\) in \(140\,\mathrm{s}\), with negligible heat loss. Estimate \(c\).
questions.answer:
The electrical energy supplied is
\[
Q=Pt=(24)(140)=3360\,\mathrm{J}
\]
The temperature change is
\[
\Delta T=30-22=8\,\mathrm{K}
\]
Thus
\[
c=\frac{Q}{m\Delta T}=\frac{3360}{(0.30)(8)}=1.4\times10^3\,\mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}\,K^{-1}}
\]

questions.prompt: Two objects have heat capacities \(C_1\) and \(C_2\). The same positive heat \(Q\) is added to each separately. Derive the ratio of their temperature changes and interpret it.
questions.answer:
For each object,
\[
\Delta T_1=\frac{Q}{C_1},\qquad \Delta T_2=\frac{Q}{C_2}
\]
Therefore
\[
\frac{\Delta T_1}{\Delta T_2}=\frac{C_2}{C_1}
\]
The object with the larger heat capacity has the smaller temperature change for the same heat input.

questions.prompt: A body with temperature-dependent heat capacity \(C(T)=C_0(1+\gamma T)\) is heated from \(T_1\) to \(T_2\). Derive the heat input \(Q\).
questions.answer:
For a temperature-dependent heat capacity,
\[
dQ=C(T)\,dT
\]
so
\[
Q=\int_{T_1}^{T_2}C_0(1+\gamma T)\,dT
\]
\[
Q=C_0\left[(T_2-T_1)+\frac{\gamma}{2}(T_2^2-T_1^2)\right]
\]

questions.prompt: A device of heat capacity \(C\) receives constant power \(P\) and loses heat at rate \(b(T-T_s)\), where \(T_s\) is surroundings temperature. Derive \(T(t)\) for initial temperature \(T(0)=T_s\), and identify the limiting temperature.
questions.answer:
Energy balance gives
\[
C\frac{dT}{dt}=P-b(T-T_s)
\]
Let \(\theta=T-T_s\). Since \(T(0)=T_s\), \(\theta(0)=0\). Then
\[
C\frac{d\theta}{dt}=P-b\theta
\]
or
\[
\frac{d\theta}{dt}+\frac{b}{C}\theta=\frac{P}{C}
\]
The solution is
\[
\theta(t)=\frac{P}{b}\left(1-e^{-bt/C}\right)
\]
so
\[
T(t)=T_s+\frac{P}{b}\left(1-e^{-bt/C}\right)
\]
The limiting temperature is
\[
T_{\infty}=T_s+\frac{P}{b}
\]
